newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium protests at another French factory closure.
newsitem.headline: Belgium protests at another French factory closure.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene wrote to Alacatel Alsthom Chairman Serge Tchuruk on Thursday to protest against the French company's plan to close a Belgian unit, the economics ministry said.
Alcatel Bell, the Belgian subsidiary of Alcatel, said earlier it would end activity at its Colfontaine plant in September, transferring almost all of it to a factory in France.
Belgium is still seething over a sudden decision by French car maker Renault to close a profitable factory in Dehaene's home town Vilvoorde in order to move production to France and Spain.
In a statement, the ministry said Dehaene was "dismayed" at the news. Economics Minister Elio Di Rupo had also contacted Tchuruk, asking the company to reconsider its decision, it said.

The Colfontaine plant, which employs 189 people, makes switches used in office telephone systems and equipment for public telephone boxes. The pay phone activities are to be moved to Turkey, the company said.
